input.rationale: Close the recorded limitation that the periodic-heartbeat batching path was source-only. The same harness now queues two follower reads and lets one ordinary leader tick produce the confirmation heartbeat, with no harness-chosen delivery order: the heartbeat carries the newest queued context, the reply to the earlier requester carries that newest context at the confirmed index, and the earlier requester's batch stays at index zero after the ready index is applied. A single-read case uses the same tick-driven path and completes, so the difference is the batching of an earlier request into a newer confirmation rather than the tick path itself. The harness file is the one used by the observer-endpoint experiment, extended with these two cases, so this is a fresh execution of a revised experiment.

scope.description: Tick-driven ReadIndex batching. Two follower-originated ReadIndex requests are queued at the real leader of a three-voter in-process group, one ordinary leader tick produces the confirmation heartbeat, and the earlier requester's reply and pending-read completion are measured; a second case queues one read and runs the same tick path.
assumptions: The voter group is three real in-process Raft Peer handlers with bootstrap membership {1,2,3}; node 1 is leader and each node uses a test-only in-memory ILogDB.
Both reads are registered through the real node-level pendingReadIndex and forwarded by the real follower ReadIndex path.
The only scheduling input is one leader tick; the harness does not choose which heartbeat is delivered first or reorder any message.
The single-read control uses the same setup, the same tick path and the same consumer, with one queued request instead of two.
Production code is unchanged.
excluded: No NodeHost, transport, persistence, restart or snapshot path is exercised.
No proposal or membership change is made while the reads are outstanding.
The run observes reply-context association and pending-read completion only; it does not attempt to establish a stale data value.

experiment.prefix: The harness launches three real Raft peers with bootstrap membership {1,2,3} and ticks node 1 until its current-term no-op is committed. Node 2 and node 3 each register a node-level pending read under a generated context and forward it to the leader through the real follower path, so both requests sit in the leader's readIndex queue. The harness then calls Tick once on the leader and pumps it; the produced heartbeat addressed to node 3 carries the newest queued context. That heartbeat is delivered to node 3, whose echo is returned to the leader, and the leader's replies are collected. The reply addressed to node 2 is emitted with its response context and log index, delivered to node 2's real handler, and the resulting ReadyToRead plus that log index are fed to pendingReadIndex.addReady and pendingReadIndex.applied; the run records the batch index and whether the read completed. The control case repeats the setup with only node 2's read queued, ticks the leader once, delivers the heartbeat carrying that single context, and records the same reply and completion fields.
experiment.requirement: A leader-produced confirmation heartbeat must not cause an earlier queued ReadIndex request to be answered with a different request's SystemCtx, and the earlier requester's admitted read must complete once the confirmed index is applied.
experiment.responsibility: leaderTick and broadcastHeartbeatMessage choose the context carried by the periodic heartbeat, handleLeaderHeartbeatResp feeds the echoed hint to handleReadIndexLeaderConfirmation, and that handler builds each remote reply; the requesting node's pendingReadIndex consumes it. The experiment exercises those real handlers and changes only how many reads are queued before the tick.

comparisons.description: When a leader tick confirms the newest of two queued reads, the reply delivered to the earlier requester must still carry the context that requester admitted.
After the confirmed index is applied, the earlier requester's admitted read should complete.
With one queued read, the tick-driven reply must carry that read's own context.
With one queued read, the same tick-driven path should complete it.

experiment.revision_reason: Add a tick-driven periodic-heartbeat case with two queued reads and a single-read control, so the batching path recorded from source is measured rather than assumed.

scope.description: Three in-process Raft peers with real Peer handlers and a test-only in-memory ILogDB. Nodes 2 and 3 issue ReadIndex requests with distinct SystemCtx values; the later context is confirmed first and the resulting reply for node 2 is routed through node 2's real follower handler and pendingReadIndex consumer.
assumptions: The three peers bootstrap membership {1,2,3}; node 1 is ticked until its current-term no-op commits.
The in-memory ILogDB preserves the ILogDB methods and indices needed for bootstrap, replication, and term lookup; it does not model disk failure, restart, or snapshots.

Both ReadIndex requests are queued at leader 1 before either heartbeat response is delivered. The later heartbeat is delivered to node 3 first, while the earlier heartbeat to node 2 is withheld. This is a controlled but ordinary reordering of same-term heartbeat responses.
The applied index for the pending batch is taken from the ReadyToRead produced by node 2's real follower handler, not invented.

No production code is modified. The client timeout is not waited for; completion is checked synchronously after applying the returned ready index, and the source pending-read timeout path remains the eventual endpoint.
excluded: No claim about every transport schedule, malicious peers, disk faults, snapshot restoration, witnesses, or observer-initiated reads.
No claim that every ReadIndex request times out; this probe concerns the demonstrated earlier-request/later-confirmation ordering.

basis.prefix: The harness launches three real internal/raft Peer instances with bootstrap membership {1,2,3} and a test-only in-memory ILogDB. Node 1 is ticked until its current-term no-op is committed. Real node 2 and node 3 Peer.ReadIndex calls create contexts A and B and forward them to leader 1. The test withholds heartbeat A to node 2, delivers heartbeat B to node 3, returns node 3's real HeartbeatResp to leader 1, and routes the leader's resulting ReadIndexResp for node 2 through node 2's real follower handler and pendingReadIndex consumer. The ReadyToRead index is then supplied as the applied index. Production logic is unchanged; message order and the in-memory log store are controlled test inputs.
basis.requirement: A follower-originated ReadIndex decision must be associated with the SystemCtx under which that follower registered the pending read, and a returned ReadyToRead at an applied index must complete that pending batch. Confirmation batching at the leader must not replace a remote request's context with another request's context.
basis.responsibility: The leader constructs remote ReadIndexResp messages in handleReadIndexLeaderConfirmation. The requesting node's pendingReadIndex consumes the returned SystemCtx and associates it with the registered batch. The test uses real Peer and pending-read handlers; it controls only message ordering and the test storage backend.

comparisons.description: The ReadIndex reply delivered to node 2 must carry the context node 2 admitted.
After the real ready index is applied, the admitted pending read should complete; zero means the response was not associated with the original batch.

scope.description: Sequential-confirmation control in the same three-peer in-process Raft group. Context A is queued before context B, but A is confirmed first; the resulting reply is routed through node 2's real follower handler and pendingReadIndex consumer.
assumptions: Real in-process Raft Peer handlers, a test-only in-memory ILogDB, and the same bootstrap membership {1,2,3} as the failing case.
Both requests are queued at the leader before confirmation. The heartbeat carrying node 2's context A is delivered to node 2 and its response returned to the leader before context B is confirmed.
The control uses the same pending-read consumer and applies the ReadyToRead index returned by node 2's follower handler.
Production code is unchanged; only message ordering and the test storage backend are controlled.
excluded: This control does not exercise disk persistence, restart, snapshots, real transport delay, or a later-confirmation race.
It is a comparison control for the main ordering case, not a separate defect claim.

basis.requirement: When the admitted context is the one confirmed first, the remote reply must carry that same SystemCtx and the applied ReadyToRead must complete the pending read through the same consumer path.

scope.description: Logical-deadline case in the same three-peer in-process harness. A later context is confirmed first, node 2 receives the wrong context, its applied ReadyToRead leaves the original batch at index zero, and the pending-read clock is advanced past the caller's deadline.
assumptions: Real in-process Raft Peer handlers, a test-only in-memory ILogDB, and bootstrap membership {1,2,3}.
Node 2's read is created with a 50-tick timeout. The test applies the returned ReadyToRead index before advancing the logical clock.
The logical clock is advanced to tick 51 and pendingReadIndex.applied is called to invoke the existing GC path; no wall-clock sleep is used.
Production code is unchanged; the result code is read from the returned RequestState and emitted as both its numeric code and name.
excluded: This case measures the logical deadline and GC path, not real wall-clock scheduling or transport delay.
It does not claim a timeout under a stable correct-context reply or under every leadership change.

basis.prefix: The harness uses the same three-peer cluster as the main and control experiments. Node 1 is ticked until its current-term no-op commits. Node 2 and node 3 queue ReadIndex contexts A and B. Heartbeat B is delivered to node 3 and its response returned to leader 1 before A is delivered to node 2. The leader's reply for node 2 carries the later context; the test routes it through node 2's real follower handler, feeds the resulting ReadyToRead to pendingReadIndex, applies the index, and observes that the original batch remains at index zero. It then advances the logical clock to 51, invokes pendingReadIndex.applied again to run GC, and reads the RequestResult.
basis.requirement: The earlier unmatched batch must remain uncompleted before the caller deadline and must yield the caller-supplied timeout result after the logical deadline; the GC path must remove the stale batch.
basis.responsibility: pendingReadIndex.gc owns the deadline timeout and batch cleanup after the response context fails to match the admitted batch. The test uses the real pending-read consumer and only advances its logical clock.

comparisons.description: After the logical deadline and the GC trigger, the unmatched pending read must return RequestTimeout.
The timeout GC path should remove the stale batch.

knowledge.assertion: A response with a nonmatching SystemCtx leaves the original pending batch at index zero and cannot complete it.

scope.description: Membership-level observer-promotion control with an observer at address a2 and AddNode targets a2, a3, and empty.
assumptions: The internal membership state machine is exercised directly with OrderedConfigChange enabled and an empty ConfigChangeId.
Each target case starts from a fresh membership containing observer 100 at a2.
The request-level target validator is source-traced but not included; this control starts at handleConfigChange.
Production code is unchanged; no execution of NodeHost or transport is included.
excluded: This control does not resolve whether the API comment or the membership guard is the intended contract.
It does not test a custom target validator or a transport-level request.

It submits an AddNode config change at index 1000 with target a2, a3, or empty, records the accepted decision and whether observer 100 remains, and compares those observations with the case expectations.
basis.requirement: The membership state machine must accept an AddNode only when it promotes the observer with the stored address; a different or empty target must not promote the observer or remove its observer role.
basis.responsibility: membership.handleConfigChange and its promotion guards own the decision; this control invokes that state machine directly and records its returns and role map.

comparisons.description: The membership accepted decision should match the target-case expectation.

scope.description: Observer-local ReadIndex endpoint. A real observer Raft peer for node 4 forwards an observer-originated ReadIndex request to the real leader of a three-voter in-process group, a later voter-originated request is queued behind it, and the leader's reply is processed by the observer's own Raft handler and the node-level pending-read registry.
assumptions: The voter group is three real in-process Raft Peer handlers with bootstrap membership {1,2,3}; node 1 is the leader and the storage backend is a test-only in-memory ILogDB.
Each voter records node 4 as an observer through Peer.ApplyConfigChange, which is the state produced by an applied AddObserver entry; the leader's ReadIndex reply path does not consult that map.
Observer 4 is a real Raft peer launched with IsObserver and a log DB carrying the committed voter membership; a leader heartbeat teaches it the current leader before it forwards a read.
The observer's SystemCtx is generated by the real node-level pendingReadIndex generator; the later voter request uses the fixed distinct context {202,2003}.
Message delivery order is controlled by the harness; both heartbeat confirmations are legal, carry the same leader term, and reach their followers only when the harness delivers them.
The control case keeps the same setup and only delivers the observer's own confirmation first.
Production code is unchanged.
excluded: No NodeHost, transport, disk persistence, restart or snapshot path is exercised.
No proposal, membership change or leader change occurs while the read is outstanding.
The run observes reply-context association and pending-read completion only; it does not attempt to establish a stale data value.

basis.prefix: The harness launches three real Raft peers with bootstrap membership {1,2,3} and ticks node 1 until its current-term no-op is committed, then records node 4 as an observer in each voter's raft membership through ApplyConfigChange. It launches observer 4 as a real observer peer whose log DB carries the committed voter membership and delivers one leader heartbeat so the observer knows its leader. The node-level pendingReadIndex registers one observer read under a generated context A and the observer peer forwards it to the leader. A later voter-originated request with context B is queued, node 3 receives its heartbeat and returns the confirmation that the leader uses to confirm B, and the leader's reply addressed to observer 4 is emitted and then handled by the observer peer. The resulting ReadyToRead output is fed to pendingReadIndex.addReady and the reply's log index to pendingReadIndex.applied, and the run records the ready index, whether the batch keyed by context A still exists and its index, and whether the client read completed. A late confirmation of context A is then delivered and checked for a context-correct reply. The control case repeats the setup, confirms context A first, and records the same completion fields.
basis.requirement: An observer-originated ReadIndex request must be answered with the SystemCtx the observer admitted, and its admitted pending read must complete once a valid ready index is applied. Confirming a later queued context first must not leave the observer's admitted batch unready after the ReadyToRead index has been applied.
basis.responsibility: handleReadIndexLeaderConfirmation constructs the remote ReadIndex reply; handleObserverReadIndex and handleFollowerReadIndex forward the observer's request; handleFollowerReadIndexResp and node.go's pendingReadIndex consume the reply and complete the read. The experiment exercises those real handlers and controls only which legal heartbeat confirmation is delivered first.

comparisons.description: When a later voter context is confirmed first, the reply delivered to observer 4 must still carry the context the observer admitted.
After the observer's real handler produced a ReadyToRead and its index was applied, the observer's admitted read should complete.
In the control, confirming the observer's own context must yield a reply carrying that context.
In the control, the observer's admitted read should complete through the same consumer path.

result.summary: Requested execution of a revised experiment that closes the recorded source-only limitation on periodic-heartbeat batching: the same harness now queues two follower reads and lets one ordinary leader tick produce the confirmation heartbeat, with no harness-chosen delivery order. Local construction runs passed and showed the heartbeat carrying the newest context, the reply to the earlier requester carrying that context at the confirmed index, and the earlier batch staying at index zero, while the single-read control completed on the same tick path. Validation reports valid with execution_requested and one experiment create; the resulting interpretation and knowledge update await the retained receipt.

scope.description: Three in-process Raft peers with real Peer handlers and a test-only in-memory ILogDB. Nodes 2 and 3 issue ReadIndex requests with distinct SystemCtx values; the later context is confirmed first and the resulting reply for node 2 is routed through node 2's real follower handler and pendingReadIndex consumer.

scope.description: Logical-deadline case in the same three-peer in-process harness. A later context is confirmed first, node 2 receives the wrong context, its applied ReadyToRead leaves the original batch at index zero, and the pending-read clock is advanced past the caller's deadline.
assumptions: Real in-process Raft Peer handlers, a test-only in-memory ILogDB, and bootstrap membership {1,2,3}.
Node 2's read is created with a 50-tick timeout. The test applies the returned ReadyToRead index before advancing the logical clock.
The logical clock is advanced to tick 51 and pendingReadIndex.applied is called to invoke the existing GC path; no wall-clock sleep is used.
Production code is unchanged; the result code is read from the returned RequestState and emitted as both its numeric code and name.
excluded: This case measures the logical deadline and GC path, not real wall-clock scheduling or transport delay.
It does not claim a timeout under a stable correct-context reply or under every leadership change.

basis.prefix: The harness uses the same three-peer cluster as the main and control experiments. Node 1 is ticked until its current-term no-op commits. basis.requirement: The earlier unmatched batch must remain uncompleted before the caller deadline and must yield the caller-supplied timeout result after the logical deadline; the GC path must remove the stale batch.

scope.description: Membership-level observer-promotion control with an observer at address a2 and AddNode targets a2, a3, and empty.

scope.description: Observer-local ReadIndex endpoint. A real observer Raft peer for node 4 forwards an observer-originated ReadIndex request to the real leader of a three-voter in-process group, a later voter-originated request is queued behind it, and the leader's reply is processed by the observer's own Raft handler and the node-level pending-read registry.

basis.prefix: The harness launches three real Raft peers with bootstrap membership {1,2,3} and ticks node 1 until its current-term no-op is committed, then records node 4 as an observer in each voter's raft membership through ApplyConfigChange. The node-level pendingReadIndex registers one observer read under a generated context A and the observer peer forwards it to the leader. A later voter-originated request with context B is queued, node 3 receives its heartbeat and returns the confirmation that the leader uses to confirm B, and the leader's reply addressed to observer 4 is emitted and then handled by the observer peer. The resulting ReadyToRead output is fed to pendingReadIndex.addReady and the reply's log index to pendingReadIndex.applied, and the run records the ready index, whether the batch keyed by context A still exists and its index, and whether the client read completed. after.description: Tick-driven ReadIndex batching. Two follower-originated ReadIndex requests are queued at the real leader of a three-voter in-process group, one ordinary leader tick produces the confirmation heartbeat, and the earlier requester's reply and pending-read completion are measured; a second case queues one read and runs the same tick path.
assumptions: The voter group is three real in-process Raft Peer handlers with bootstrap membership {1,2,3}; node 1 is leader and each node uses a test-only in-memory ILogDB.
Both reads are registered through the real node-level pendingReadIndex and forwarded by the real follower ReadIndex path.
The only scheduling input is one leader tick; the harness does not choose which heartbeat is delivered first or reorder any message.
The single-read control uses the same setup, the same tick path and the same consumer, with one queued request instead of two.
Production code is unchanged.
excluded: No NodeHost, transport, persistence, restart or snapshot path is exercised.
No proposal or membership change is made while the reads are outstanding.
The run observes reply-context association and pending-read completion only; it does not attempt to establish a stale data value.

prefix.before: The harness launches three real Raft peers with bootstrap membership {1,2,3} and ticks node 1 until its current-term no-op is committed, then records node 4 as an observer in each voter's raft membership through ApplyConfigChange. It launches observer 4 as a real observer peer whose log DB carries the committed voter membership and delivers one leader heartbeat so the observer knows its leader. The node-level pendingReadIndex registers one observer read under a generated context A and the observer peer forwards it to the leader. A later voter-originated request with context B is queued, node 3 receives its heartbeat and returns the confirmation that the leader uses to confirm B, and the leader's reply addressed to observer 4 is emitted and then handled by the observer peer. The resulting ReadyToRead output is fed to pendingReadIndex.addReady and the reply's log index to pendingReadIndex.applied, and the run records the ready index, whether the batch keyed by context A still exists and its index, and whether the client read completed. A late confirmation of context A is then delivered and checked for a context-correct reply. The control case repeats the setup, confirms context A first, and records the same completion fields.
prefix.after: The harness launches three real Raft peers with bootstrap membership {1,2,3} and ticks node 1 until its current-term no-op is committed. Node 2 and node 3 each register a node-level pending read under a generated context and forward it to the leader through the real follower path, so both requests sit in the leader's readIndex queue. The harness then calls Tick once on the leader and pumps it; the produced heartbeat addressed to node 3 carries the newest queued context. That heartbeat is delivered to node 3, whose echo is returned to the leader, and the leader's replies are collected. The reply addressed to node 2 is emitted with its response context and log index, delivered to node 2's real handler, and the resulting ReadyToRead plus that log index are fed to pendingReadIndex.addReady and pendingReadIndex.applied; the run records the batch index and whether the read completed. The control case repeats the setup with only node 2's read queued, ticks the leader once, delivers the heartbeat carrying that single context, and records the same reply and completion fields.

requirement.before: An observer-originated ReadIndex request must be answered with the SystemCtx the observer admitted, and its admitted pending read must complete once a valid ready index is applied. Confirming a later queued context first must not leave the observer's admitted batch unready after the ReadyToRead index has been applied.
requirement.after: A leader-produced confirmation heartbeat must not cause an earlier queued ReadIndex request to be answered with a different request's SystemCtx, and the earlier requester's admitted read must complete once the confirmed index is applied.

responsibility.before: handleReadIndexLeaderConfirmation constructs the remote ReadIndex reply; handleObserverReadIndex and handleFollowerReadIndex forward the observer's request; handleFollowerReadIndexResp and node.go's pendingReadIndex consume the reply and complete the read. The experiment exercises those real handlers and controls only which legal heartbeat confirmation is delivered first.
responsibility.after: leaderTick and broadcastHeartbeatMessage choose the context carried by the periodic heartbeat, handleLeaderHeartbeatResp feeds the echoed hint to handleReadIndexLeaderConfirmation, and that handler builds each remote reply; the requesting node's pendingReadIndex consumes it. The experiment exercises those real handlers and changes only how many reads are queued before the tick.

before.description: When a later voter context is confirmed first, the reply delivered to observer 4 must still carry the context the observer admitted.
After the observer's real handler produced a ReadyToRead and its index was applied, the observer's admitted read should complete.
In the control, confirming the observer's own context must yield a reply carrying that context.
In the control, the observer's admitted read should complete through the same consumer path.

after.description: When a leader tick confirms the newest of two queued reads, the reply delivered to the earlier requester must still carry the context that requester admitted.
After the confirmed index is applied, the earlier requester's admitted read should complete.
With one queued read, the tick-driven reply must carry that read's own context.
With one queued read, the same tick-driven path should complete it.

experiments.revision_reason: Add a tick-driven periodic-heartbeat case with two queued reads and a single-read control, so the batching path recorded from source is measured rather than assumed.
